blocks.title: *"i'll think about it"* is almost never about thinking

blocks.text: a sales legend explained why, back in 1984.

blocks.label: zig ziglar, secrets of closing the sale, 1984

blocks.lead: "There are five basic reasons people will not buy from you. These are: no need, no money, no hurry, no desire, and no trust."

blocks.text:
42 years later, your DMs still hit all five. they just come with emojis now.

here's what each one looks like in an inbox, and the one question i'd ask.

chat.text: that's totally fair, what made you click today?

blocks.text: they don't see the problem yet. so i'd let them say it in their own words.

chat.text: it's $1,500, or 3 payments of $550. what result are you hoping for?

blocks.text: a price alone sounds expensive. a price next to their goal sounds like a plan.

chat.text: that makes total sense. what happens if nothing changes by then?

blocks.text: no hurry usually means no deadline. a gentle question gives them one, without pushing.

chat.text: sounds cool, i'll check it out
thanks for checking it out! what have you already tried so far?

blocks.text: "cool" is polite for "meh". find out what they want before you pitch what you have.

chat.text: is this actually legit? i've been burned before
totally fair, thanks for saying it. what happened last time?

blocks.text: never argue with a bad experience. answer the worry first, then listen.

blocks.caption: these are example replies, adapt them to your offer, your price and your voice.

blocks.title: the fix is never a better pitch. it's a better *question*

blocks.heading: which one do you hear the *most*?
